sources.locator: "Spanish colonization of the Americas", revision 1376245871, § The conquest of Mexico

explanation: The expedition that became the conquest of Mexico set out from a colony that was already there, and the article says so in its own words: **"A well-connected settler in Cuba, Hernán Cortés received authorization in 1519 by the governor of Cuba to form an expedition of exploration-only to this far western region."** Twenty-six years of settlement in the Caribbean — the article gives the Spanish over two decades of exploring the islands and the mainland coast before this — are what put a governor in Havana with expeditions to license and a settler with the standing to lead one. The conquest is also filed as part of the colonization, which is a different statement: this link claims the licence and the base it came from, not that the colonization made the conquest inevitable.
